newsitem.title: MOROCCO: Morocco's Samir turnover down in H1.
newsitem.headline: Morocco's Samir turnover down in H1.

text.p: Morocco's Samir oil refinery announced on Thursday a drop of 3.9 percent in turnover to 3.210 billion dirhams ($368.9 million) in the first half of the year compared with the same period in 1995.
It registered a turnover of 3.341 billion dirhams in January-June 1995, it said in its half-year report.
The country's main refinery, Samir said it posted a net profit of 262.9 million dirhams in the first half of 1996 but gave no comparative figures for the same period in 1995.
Market analysts said it was the first time the refinery had published its half-year results since it was partly privatised in March 1996.
The government floated 30 percent of the refinery on the Casablanca bourse at 243 dirhams a share, or the equivalent of a total $310 million.
The Societe Marocaine de l'Industrie du Raffinage (Samir), located in Mohammedia near Casablanca, has a capital of 1.03 billion dirhams.
Samir refines 80 percent of the country's average 6.0 million tonnes of crude imports every year.
"Samir's turnover decline is due largely to a drop in domestic oil sales," a Casablanca-based stockbroker said.
The government expects to sell up to a 51 percent stake to foreign oil investors by end-1996.
One of the country's 46 listed stocks, Samir's shares were last traded at 252 dirhams.
